name: Resistance Band Chest Fly
description: The resistance band chest fly is a portable, joint-friendly isolation exercise that trains the pectoral muscles through a wide arc using an elastic band. As the band stretches, resistance increases toward peak contraction, providing an accommodating load curve that complements the natural strength curve of the chest.

execution.starting_position: Anchor a resistance band behind you at chest height or loop it around a stable post. Stand facing away and hold one end of the band in each hand, arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height.
execution.setup_instructions: Secure the band anchor at chest height. Step far enough from the anchor that the band has light tension even at the start position.
steps: Step 1: Stand in a staggered or athletic stance, holding both ends of the band.
Step 2: Begin with arms extended out to the sides, hands at shoulder level.
Step 3: Sweep both arms forward and together in front of your chest, squeezing the pectorals at the meeting point.
Step 4: Slowly open the arms back to the starting position with control, resisting the band's pull.
Step 5: Maintain a fixed, slightly bent elbow throughout the movement.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you bring the arms together. Inhale as you open them back to the start.
common_mistakes: Anchoring the band too low or too high, altering the exercise angle
Allowing the arms to snap back due to band recoil
Straightening the elbows completely under tension
safety_considerations: Check the band anchor is secure before each set
Inspect bands for tears or wear before use
Start with a lighter band to establish range of motion
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Open arms until a mild chest stretch is felt. Bring hands together without crossing the midline past the sternum for maximum contraction.
coaching_cues: Control the band on the way back — it's the eccentric that builds
Feel the chest squeeze as hands meet
